reviewer.affiliation: OpenAI Codex, commissioned by the Wirestack repository owner
reviewer.independenceStatement: I reviewed the immutable no-history snapshot without implementation context or production changes. I checked source, exact evidence bytes, the refreshed pinned-SDK M3-030 task record, and bounded negative tests instead of trusting prior PASS labels.
conflicts: The repository owner commissioned this process-isolated Codex verifier through the implementation orchestrator.
Process isolation is not organizational independence from an external security firm.
The snapshot has no Git metadata, so I could not independently query tracked-file state, branch protection, or remote GitHub state.

findings.title: Canonical TLS provider manifest was missing
findings.reproduction: Start a standard CJPM lifecycle from repository inputs.
findings.impact: The provider build was not reproducible without the manifest.
findings.evidence: The exact AWS-LC pin is present and validated. Preserved clean-checkout evidence is digest-bound; the no-history snapshot cannot test Git tracking.
findings.fix: Track and validate the canonical AWS-LC manifest.

regressions.command: python3 -m unittest focused M7-029 build, release, and supply-chain contracts -v

findings.dispositionRationale: Manifest parsing, exact pin checks, and preserved clean-checkout regression evidence close the missing-input failure.

findings.title: Pull requests lacked a required clean Cangjie gate
findings.reproduction: Inspect the pull-request workflow and preserved ruleset observation.
findings.impact: Broken native inputs or Cangjie sources could merge behind partial checks.
findings.evidence: The workflow runs the clean gate. Digest-bound evidence records a successful hosted job and strict required status with no bypass actors.
findings.fix: Add the hosted clean build and require it on main.
findings.dispositionRationale: The local workflow and preserved remote observation agree. Remote state was not re-queried.

findings.title: CJPM hook omitted the resolver archive
findings.reproduction: Run cjpm check with resolver output absent.
findings.impact: A clean lifecycle could build TLS but fail for a missing resolver archive.
findings.evidence: Every CJPM phase calls the combined native builder; the exact missing-resolver reproduction is preserved and digest-bound.
findings.fix: Build provider and resolver inputs from one pre-phase hook.

regressions.command: codex_cangjie_env cjpm check with target/native/resolver absent

findings.dispositionRationale: The prior failure precondition now succeeds.

findings.title: Qualification freshness omitted native and build inputs
findings.reproduction: Mutate a release-critical native or build input and validate old qualification.
findings.impact: Stale release evidence could appear current.
findings.evidence: Qualification covers manifests, native sources, builders, lockfile, hook, selection, and ABI contract. Supply-chain fingerprints propagate embedded archive and manifest identities.
findings.fix: Bind every release-critical native and build control into qualification and fingerprints.

regressions.command: python3 -m unittest focused M7-029 build, release, and supply-chain contracts -v

findings.dispositionRationale: Current code invalidates stale evidence after input drift. Final-candidate regeneration remains WS-EVID-002.

findings.title: Main lacked required checks and protection
findings.reproduction: Query repository rulesets and default-branch protection.
findings.impact: Direct or non-fast-forward updates could bypass security controls.
findings.evidence: Digest-bound evidence records strict required checks, deletion and non-fast-forward prohibitions, and no bypass actors.
findings.fix: Activate a strict main ruleset requiring the clean hosted gate.
findings.dispositionRationale: The preserved observation closes the finding, but this review did not refresh remote state.

findings.title: Server consumed DATA credit before queue admission
findings.reproduction: Force reserved DATA enqueue to fail and inspect both credits.
findings.impact: Failed admission could starve sibling streams.
findings.evidence: Reservation ownership transfers through enqueueReservedData and failure cancels it; the scheduler regression is digest-bound.
findings.fix: Transfer the permit atomically to the writer.
findings.dispositionRationale: Permit transfer and failure cleanup are one writer operation.

findings.title: Peer defaults and local SETTINGS were conflated
findings.reproduction: Use non-default local receive limits and inspect initial peer state and SETTINGS.
findings.impact: Peers could disagree on frame, window, table, or stream limits.
findings.evidence: RFC peer defaults, local caps, and advertised settings are separate; focused evidence is digest-bound.
findings.fix: Separate settings roles and advertise finite non-default receive limits.
findings.dispositionRationale: State and wire advertisement now match their protocol roles.

findings.title: Cancellation wrapper changed H2 completion semantics
findings.reproduction: Read declared bytes before delayed H2 END_STREAM or trailers through the wrapper.
findings.impact: The wrapper could detach cancellation and complete early.
findings.evidence: The wrapper copies completesAtDeclaredLength from its delegate; facade evidence is digest-bound.
findings.dispositionRationale: Protocol EOF remains the completion event for wrapped H2 bodies.

findings.title: Release lacked a project license grant
findings.reproduction: Inspect root licenses, payload inventory, and SPDX metadata.
findings.impact: Downstream use and redistribution rights were unclear.
findings.evidence: The Apache-2.0 grant, AWS-LC notices, and SPDX license checks are present.
findings.fix: Ship the project grant and exact third-party notices and bind them into metadata.

regressions.command: python3 -m unittest focused release license and SBOM tests -v

findings.dispositionRationale: Source and release contracts now carry the grant and attribution.

findings.title: CONNECT pooling omitted proxy credential identity
findings.reproduction: Rotate dynamic proxy credentials for the same proxy and origin.
findings.impact: A tunnel authenticated as one principal could serve another.
findings.evidence: Dynamic authenticated CONNECT tunnels are single lease; proxy regression evidence is digest-bound.
findings.fix: Disable reuse when no stable credential partition exists.
findings.dispositionRationale: Rotated credentials cannot share an authenticated tunnel.

findings.title: Blocked getaddrinfo could make resolver teardown unbounded
findings.reproduction: Block each pool, release handles, exceed the process cap, then release calls and retry.
findings.impact: Closed pools could retain unbounded workers and memory behind libc or NSS.
findings.evidence: The native gate proves bounded overload and later admission after safe reaping; its report is digest-bound.
findings.fix: Reserve process-wide capacity, quarantine stuck pools, fail closed at the cap, and release capacity only after reaping.
findings.dispositionRationale: Uninterruptible calls may remain quarantined, but total pools and workers are bounded process-wide.

findings.title: Ambiguous physical write timeout was retryable
findings.reproduction: Timeout after entering a physical write without zero-byte commit proof.
findings.impact: Automatic retry could duplicate a request.
findings.evidence: Physical write timeout maps to Retryability.Never; transport regression evidence is digest-bound.
findings.fix: Treat unknown physical commit state as non-retryable.
findings.dispositionRationale: The default cannot resend an ambiguously committed write.

findings.title: Cancelling one accept closed the listener
findings.reproduction: Cancel one pending accept, then accept a later connection.
findings.impact: One request could terminate the service listener.
findings.evidence: Accept uses operation-scoped bounded waits; transport regression evidence proves listener reuse.
findings.fix: Separate operation cancellation from listener lifetime.
findings.dispositionRationale: Only explicit close terminates the listener.

findings.title: Trust changes did not alter TLS session partition
findings.reproduction: Replace a same-size bundle or hashed-directory certificate and compare trust identity.
findings.impact: Old sessions could be offered after trust replacement.
findings.evidence: Bounded deterministic SHA-256 identities cover bundle and directory contents; adapter evidence is digest-bound.
findings.fix: Bind session trust identity to selected trust-store contents.
findings.dispositionRationale: Trust replacement changes the session partition.

findings.title: Native ABI contract omitted production Cangjie imports
findings.reproduction: Delete a production import from the contract or a required archive symbol and validate selection.
findings.impact: A provider could pass while omitting a production function.
findings.evidence: Schema v2 inventories 56 production imports and signatures. Current negative tests reject incomplete inventory and missing symbols. The refreshed pinned-SDK task-check records all six M3-030 commands PASS.
findings.fix: Require exact production-import, signature, and archive-symbol coverage.
findings.dispositionRationale: Current contract coverage, negative tests, archive checks, and the regenerated pinned-20260817 task record close the omission path.

findings.title: Name-only ABI validation accepted incompatible prototypes
findings.reproduction: Mutate Cangjie types, native header prototypes, schema, calling convention, or signature inventory.
findings.impact: An ABI-incompatible provider could corrupt arguments or return values.
findings.evidence: The contract records return and parameter types plus C convention. Current negative tests reject Cangjie, native-header, schema, convention, and inventory mutations. A C11 function-pointer probe promotes incompatible-pointer warnings to errors.
findings.fix: Validate signatures at both Cangjie-contract and contract-header boundaries.
findings.dispositionRationale: Independent negative tests and the exact refreshed pinned-SDK task record reject every reviewed signature mismatch before provider use.

findings.title: Final-candidate release evidence is not regenerated
findings.reproduction: Compare M7-021 and M7-025 package states with the current source and ABI contract.
findings.impact: Historical release and SBOM outputs do not prove final-candidate identity or long-running behavior.
findings.evidence: The package marks affected release, SBOM, audit, installation, and performance rows STALE_AFTER_M7_032 or HISTORICAL_NON_GATING.
findings.dispositionRationale: Keep open until final-candidate artifacts and required long profiles are regenerated. This Medium limitation is not a High or Critical M7-029 blocker.
